section-130: Meaning and importance: ECCE refers to care, health, nutrition and education of children from birth to about eight years. Since most brain development happens in these years, quality ECCE improves school readiness, learning, health and later life outcomes, and reduces inequality.
Objectives: Holistic physical, emotional, social, language, cognitive and creative development, development of good habits and self-help skills, and smooth transition to primary school.

Policy perspectives: The National Policy on Education 1986 described ECCE as a crucial input for primary education and recommended a play-based, holistic approach integrated with ICDS and day-care centres. The Yash Pal Committee (1993) recommended abolition of tests and interviews for admission, no formal teaching or homework at the pre-primary stage and use of the mother tongue. NEP 2020 includes three years of pre-school in the Foundational Stage.
Agencies and services: ICDS/Anganwadis, ICCW, CSWB, government pre-primary sections, NGOs and private nursery schools provide services such as nutrition, health, crèches and pre-school education.
section-131: Nursery schools: Developed by the McMillan sisters, nursery schools provide care, health, play and social experiences for children aged about 2 to 5 in a homely environment.
Kindergarten: Froebel's kindergarten (1837) treats the school as a garden and the teacher as a gardener. It uses gifts, occupations, songs, games and stories, emphasising self-activity and play.

Montessori: Maria Montessori's Children's House (1907) uses a prepared environment, self-correcting didactic apparatus, exercises of practical life and sense training. The child learns through auto-education while the teacher observes and guides.

Anganwadi: The Anganwadi centre under ICDS provides supplementary nutrition, immunisation, health check-ups, referral services, pre-school education and health and nutrition education. It is the largest ECCE system in India and is being strengthened under NEP 2020 and Mission Poshan 2.0.
section-132: Meaning: Programme planning in ECCE is the organisation of goals, activities, materials, space and time so that young children develop holistically.
Principles: Plans should be child-centred, developmentally appropriate, play-based, holistic, flexible, balanced, inclusive, based on local culture and resources, and should involve parents.

Types of planning: Long-term planning sets yearly or term goals and themes; theme-based short-term planning links activities in language, numeracy, art, science and social skills around a theme for a week or a few days. A daily routine balances free play, group time, outdoor play, meals, rest and stories.

Materials: Low-cost and no-cost materials made from waste and local resources - boxes, bottle caps, seeds, cloth, leaves and clay - make ECCE affordable and encourage creativity and environmental awareness.
section-133: Importance of play: Play is the natural way young children learn. It develops the body, mind, language, emotions and social skills, and gives joy and confidence.
Meeting personal needs: Activities and routines that develop self-help skills like handwashing, eating, dressing and toilet habits build independence and good health habits.
Language activities: Storytelling and nursery rhymes develop listening, vocabulary, imagination, memory, rhythm and moral values. Children can retell, dramatise and sing along.

Play with and without materials: Play with blocks, clay, puzzles, sand, water and art materials develops fine motor skills, concepts and creativity; play without materials - running, dancing, action songs, imitation and traditional games - develops gross motor skills, cooperation and rule-following. A good ECCE programme uses both types in a balanced way.
